songs.name: And We Bid You Good Night

ai_show_review.summary: Monumental Dark Star with high‑energy Mason’s Children, crisp SBD
ai_show_review.blurb: The set is anchored by a soaring Dark Star that showcases Jerry’s stellar tone, followed by a tight transition into Saint Stephen and Mason’s Children. Good Lovin’ and Uncle John’s Band round out a high‑energy performance. The soundboard capture is crystal clear, making this early‑70s show a standout gem.
ai_show_review.review: On February 2, 1970 at St. Louis’ Fox Theatre the Dead delivered an unforgettable early‑70s statement. After a solid opening stretch of classics, the band launched into a monumental Dark Star that has been described as “beautiful,” “smoking” and “transcendent.” Garcia’s lead work shines throughout, while Phil Lesh’s bass underpins the improvisation with inspired, lock‑step grooves. The jam segues seamlessly into Saint Stephen and then bursts into the high‑octane Mason’s Children, a transition reviewers call fluid and evidence of the group “clearly on a roll.” The set continues with a spirited Good Lovin’ and an exuberant Uncle John’s Band before winding down through two turns of Turn On Your Lovelight and a gentle And We Bid You Good Night. Across all six soundboard sources the audio is praised for its crystal‑clear, balanced mix—especially the Vernon SBD, which captures every nuance of the performance with excellent resolution despite a brief cut in Mason’s Children. This show stands out as a peak‑era snapshot of the Dead’s early ’70s evolution.

best_recording.reason: Excellent soundboard with crystal‑clear, balanced mix; captures the full Dark Star and Mason’s Children with only a minor cut, making it the clearest representation of the show.

key_highlights: Dark Star – a 45‑minute epic that anchors the entire performance
Seamless Saint Stephen → Mason's Children transition showcases high energy
Good Lovin' and Uncle John's Band deliver a powerful, uplifting finish
Crystal‑clear soundboard capture preserves early ’70 intensity

band_performance.Jerry: Garcia delivers a breathtaking Dark Star solo with beautiful tone, described as smoking and transcendent, anchoring the show.
band_performance.Phil: Lesh’s bass is inspired and locks in tightly, contributing to the ‘perfect’ band feel noted by reviewers.
band_performance.Bob: Weir adds strong rhythm work and shines during key moments of the long Dark Star jam.
